column1: # (internal/storage/store/full_row_write_guard_test.go). Each row is one site the guard finds:
# a whole-row write (GORM Save, or Select("*") + Updates) of a security-state model in
# internal/storage/store, or a caller in internal/core / internal/storage/store of a LocalStorage
# method that does one. Classified 2026-10-04 against main + every open race-fix PR merged,
# reading the callees down to the SQL issued and testing each "safe" claim against a concrete
#   UNSAFE-OPEN          a real stale-write race; the reason names the tracking issue. The row stays
#                        (removing it turns the guard red without fixing anything) until the fix
#                        makes the write column-scoped and the guard stops finding the site.
#   SAFE-STATE-CAS       Select("*") under WHERE state=?, and no writer changes another column of
#                        the row without also moving state (so a concurrent writer always makes this
#                        CAS match 0 rows); no soft delete to resurrect.
#   SAFE-ROW-LOCKED      read and write share one transaction with the row locked (FOR UPDATE, or an
#   SAFE-MONOTONE        every interleaving ends in the state this write sets (e.g. toward revoked).
#   SAFE-AS-USED         safe for its only current caller; a new caller needs re-review.
#   SAFE-LINEARIZABLE    the overwrite is equivalent to some serial order of the racing operations.
# `pending: #N` = the site disappears when race-fix PR #N merges (delete the row then);
# `ahead: #N` = the site appears when #N merges (pre-added so main stays green; drop the marker
# then). Both carry expires=2026-10-18 and are exempt from the stale-row check.
# reviewed_by must be non-empty and name a different session than added_by.
